items.title: Judge tosses Trump’s lawsuit against Wall Street Journal again, this time for good
items.brief: A federal judge on Saturday dismissed President Donald Trump’s defamation lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal over its reporting on a lewd birthday letter to Jeffrey Epstein bearing Trump’s name.

items.brief: Prime Minister Donald Tusk said on Saturday that his government would press ahead with efforts to restore the independence of Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal, as hundreds of protesters gathered for a second night…

items.title: Protests spread to Germany as hundreds of thousands march again in France
items.brief: Cost-of-living protests that began in France have spread to Germany where demonstrations to coincide with Halloween were underway on Saturday, with tens of thousands of people turning out across the country.

items.title: On Day of the Dead, tourists bump shoulders with celebrating families in San Andrés Mixquic
items.brief: As night falls over the cemetery in San Andrés Mixquic, a historic village on the outskirts of Mexico City, the family of Ángel Jiménez del Águila huddles around his grave.

items.title: 1 dead, 6 wounded in targeted shooting at California Spirit Halloween store, police say
items.brief: One person was killed and six others injured after a shooting inside a shopping mall at a Spirit Halloween store in Fairfield, California, on Friday night, police said.

items.title: Michigan man charged with threatening to kill FBI Director Kash Patel
items.brief: A Michigan man was arrested Friday and charged with making threats against FBI Director Kash Patel, federal prosecutors announced.

items.title: Judge imposes sweeping emergency order halting DOJ pressure campaign on election officials across the country
items.brief: A federal judge imposed a sweeping emergency order halting various aggressive tactics employed by the Trump administration in recent days to pressure election officials across the country.
